cards.question: Tell us about a time you had to manage multiple competing priorities.

star.situation: Working in facility maintenance, especially in healthcare and recreation, there were many days where reactive maintenance, scheduled preventative maintenance, contractor coordination and customer requests all competed for attention.
star.task: My responsibility was to ensure critical work was completed without losing sight of longer-term priorities or impacting customer service.
star.action: I started by assessing each task based on safety, operational impact and urgency. I communicated changes with stakeholders, adjusted schedules when necessary, delegated work where appropriate and continued to reassess priorities throughout the day as new issues arose.
star.result: Critical issues were addressed quickly while planned work continued to move forward. Clear communication helped manage expectations, reduced frustration and ensured resources were focused where they created the most value.

cards.question: Tell us about a process you improved.

star.situation: Throughout my career I've noticed that many recurring problems weren't caused by people—they were caused by inconsistent systems or missing information.
star.task: Rather than repeatedly fixing the same issues, I wanted to improve the underlying process.
star.action: That mindset eventually led me to begin developing Helix, an operations platform focused on organizing information, improving communication, documenting procedures and making it easier to plan maintenance and projects. Even on a smaller scale, I've consistently standardized documentation, organized workflows and looked for ways to reduce wasted effort.
star.result: The biggest improvement wasn't just efficiency—it was consistency. Better systems reduce mistakes, improve communication and allow teams to spend more time solving meaningful problems instead of searching for information.

cards.question: Tell us about a project you're proud of.

star.situation: One of the projects I'm most proud of has been developing Helix during my own time after identifying common operational challenges across multiple organizations.
star.task: My goal was to build a platform that would centralize procedures, inspections, work management, inventory and operational knowledge into one system.
star.action: I researched operational workflows, designed the platform, learned new software tools and continuously refined the concept based on real maintenance challenges I had experienced throughout my career.
star.result: Although it's still evolving, the project demonstrates how I approach problems. Rather than accepting inefficient processes, I'm motivated to build long-term solutions that improve operations and help teams succeed.

cards.question: Tell us about technology you've implemented.

star.situation: I've always been comfortable learning new technology, particularly when it can improve operational efficiency.
star.task: When existing tools didn't fully meet operational needs, I wanted to create something that better supported maintenance teams.
star.action: I taught myself new software platforms, explored different technologies and began building Helix to manage procedures, projects, inspections and operational information. Throughout my career I've also adapted quickly to new CMMS platforms and software with minimal training.
star.result: Technology has become one of my strengths because I focus on how it supports people rather than simply implementing software. My goal is always to simplify work, improve communication and provide better information for decision making.

cards.question: Describe your experience with CMMS systems.

star.situation: I've worked with several maintenance management systems throughout my career in different industries.
star.task: Each organization relied on accurate work orders, maintenance history and asset information to plan work effectively.
star.action: I've used systems such as eMaint, Archibus and RFAM while also gaining experience understanding how maintenance data supports planning and decision making. More recently I've been applying those lessons while designing Helix with a focus on usability and operational value.
star.result: Although every system is different, I've found the principles remain the same: accurate information, preventative maintenance, planning and continuous improvement.

cards.question: What is preventive maintenance and why is it important?

star.situation: Across healthcare, recreation and industrial environments, equipment reliability directly affects operations, safety and customer experience.
star.task: The objective of preventative maintenance is to reduce failures before they occur.
star.action: I believe effective preventative maintenance starts with understanding critical assets, scheduling work proactively, documenting findings, tracking trends and making adjustments based on equipment condition and operational history.
star.result: When preventative maintenance is done well, organizations experience fewer unexpected failures, safer workplaces, lower lifecycle costs and more reliable service for customers and the community.

cards.question: What does asset management mean to you?

star.situation: As I've progressed into leadership, I've become increasingly interested in how organizations manage assets over their entire lifecycle.
star.task: Rather than simply repairing equipment when it fails, I wanted to better understand long-term planning and decision making.
star.action: I've started formal asset management training while applying those principles in my own thinking. To me, asset management means balancing risk, cost, performance and service levels throughout the life of an asset while using good information to make proactive decisions.
star.result: That mindset supports more sustainable operations, better budgeting, improved reliability and ultimately better service for the public.

star.situation: Throughout my career I've worked alongside contractors on maintenance activities and projects in several industries.
star.task: My role has been to ensure work was completed safely, met quality expectations and aligned with operational requirements.
star.action: I focus on establishing clear expectations, communicating scope, coordinating schedules, confirming safety requirements and maintaining open communication throughout the project. I also believe in treating contractors as partners while still holding them accountable to agreed standards.
star.result: That approach helps reduce misunderstandings, improves safety and contributes to projects being completed efficiently and professionally.

star.situation: While I haven't directly managed departmental budgets, I've consistently worked in environments where cost awareness was important.
star.task: My responsibility has been to make sound decisions regarding materials, purchasing and resource utilization while supporting operational goals.
star.action: I've been involved in obtaining quotes, planning material requirements, considering lifecycle costs and ensuring resources were used responsibly. I also recognize that maintenance decisions often have significant financial implications beyond the immediate repair.
star.result: Although formal budgeting is an area I'd like to continue developing, I'm comfortable learning financial processes and understand the importance of balancing operational needs with responsible stewardship of public resources.

cards.question: Tell us about your approach to safety.

star.situation: Working in healthcare, recreation and especially oil and gas reinforced that safety isn't a checklist—it's a culture.
star.task: My responsibility has always been to ensure every member of the team, contractors and the public return home safely at the end of the day.
star.action: I approach every task using the Hierarchy of Controls, beginning with eliminating hazards where possible before relying on administrative controls or PPE. I encourage open communication, proper planning, hazard assessments and speaking up whenever something doesn't feel right. I also believe leaders set the standard by consistently modeling safe behaviours.
star.result: That mindset creates an environment where safety becomes part of everyday decision making rather than something people think about only during formal meetings. Strong safety cultures also lead to better teamwork, higher quality work and more reliable operations.
